Kimberly — quick technical summary below (happy to expand into the runbook):

Supported export targets (Private):
- Splunk HEC (HTTPS) — preferred for telemetry and JSON payloads; supports token-based auth and TLS client certs.
- Syslog (TLS) — RFC5424 over TLS, for traditional SIEM collectors.
- S3-compatible push (signed uploads) — for batch export and long-term retention; customer-managed bucket recommended.
- Push-to-forwarder (on-prem agent) — our forwarder can deliver to local collectors if egress is prohibited; supports mTLS and local buffering.

Proof/evidence and retention:
- Delivery receipts: HEC returns timestamps and event counts; we persist delivery logs in the control plane audit log (read-only bundle for customer).
- Signed export manifests: when using S3 exports we generate a signed manifest (SHA256) plus per-archive checksums — suitable for auditors.
- Retention enforcement: on S3 exports retention is driven by the bucket lifecycle; for HEC/syslog direct-forward we provide a signed delivery log and can snapshot a short-lived delivery archive for compliance review.

Egress & controls:
- mTLS between components (mutual certs) + client cert rotation API.
- IP allowlists and VPC endpoints; for private installs we support static egress IPs via NAT pool.
- Token rotation for HEC with short TTL and revocation endpoints exposed to a customer-managed control plane.

Limitations / notes:
- Air-gapped installs: full disconnected mode supports local forwarder + evidence bundle creation; requires offline transfer workflow for auditors (we produce an encrypted bundle).
- Seven-year retention is possible via S3 export to a customer bucket (they must guarantee lifecycle). We can provide the signed manifests and chain-of-custody logs for each export period.

I've attached the SIEM mapping template we typically use. Jonas, I'll coordinate on the runbook steps for a validation exercise.

Best,

Subject: RE: Private SIEM export and retention requirements — proposed validation runbook

Thanks — draft validation runbook and artifact list below (high level):

1) Onboarding meeting (30m)
   - Confirm export target (HEC vs syslog vs S3) and connectivity constraints.
   - Agree on retention window and evidence requirements.

2) Configuration phase (customer + Redwood):
   - Exchange certs / configure mTLS or HEC token.
   - Deploy forwarder (if needed) and enable prefix/KV caching so telemetry doesn't stall for limited egress.

3) Test export (3 steps):
   - Small-volume test (10k events) — verify delivery receipt and counts in control plane.
   - Integrity check — compare SHA256 checksums for S3 archives or HEC event counts.
   - Tracing hooks validation — generate a traced request, confirm span IDs and sampling metadata are present in exported payloads.

4) Evidence package generation:
   - Delivery logs (signed), export manifests (signed), control-plane audit snapshot (read-only), certificate chain, and a short writeup explaining retention lifecycle.
   - For air-gapped installs we produce an encrypted evidence bundle and ship via a secure transfer method.

5) Auditor handoff (we provide a drive link with read-only artifacts and an accompanying checklist).

Timeline: 1–2 weeks for standard installs (HEC/syslog). Air-gapped or heavily restricted installs can be 3–6 weeks depending on transfer cadence.

Attachments: I attached the redwood-obsv-reqs doc with the artifact templates and a short checklist.

Jonas
